title: Interpretation Rules (Tier 2)
description: Schema for the Tier-2 signal-mapping config that translates descriptive evidence labels emitted by cards into per-modality signals consumed by the Tier-3 synthesis layer. Consolidates normative knowledge that previously lived scattered across (a) card_spec interpretation_hints[].dominant flags, (b) modality-module killer_conditions, and (c) the synthesis-layer NOT_INFORMATIVE_CALLS set. Reviewable by domain experts in PR; version-controlled with the contracts. Phase 4 (2026-07-15): extended with target-first signal channels, tier metadata, list-typed field matching via in_record, and signal-absence not_applicable enum. All extensions backward-compatible.

axis.description: The biology axis this rules file applies to. Matches the dashboard_spec's axis_resolution outputs. `combination_opportunity` + `resistance_emergence` + `combinatorial_dependency` + `chemical_synergy` + `cis_coherence` are DEDICATED self-contained axes (combo-and-resistance / combination-and-vulnerability / combinatorial-dependency / cis-feature-coherence skills) — kept out of the shared nomination ladder; their rules_loader requires the file axis to equal the skill's requested axis name (so the axis must match the filename). `cis_coherence` is VERDICT-INERT at the composed target-profile layer (not registered in the skills gating axes).

rules.description: Ordered list of evidence→signal mappings. Each rule fires when its predicate matches a card's emitted descriptive label; emits a per-channel signal vector. Multiple matching rules accumulate signals.

rationale.description: Optional free-text explanation of the rules file's design intent.

signal_vocabulary.description: Controlled signal vocabulary. 'supportive' = evidence consistent. 'opposing' = evidence against. 'killer' = hard gate to not_viable (Tier-3 deterministic). 'neutral' = informational, no fit-level effect. 'insufficient' = evidence in-scope but weak/missing (coverage gap). 'not_applicable' (Phase 4, 2026-07-15) = evidence out-of-scope for this rule's tier — semantically distinct from 'insufficient' per resolver-product design.

modality_id.description: Legacy modality-only channel enum, retained for backward compatibility with pre-Phase-4 rules files.

signal_channel_id.description: Phase 4 (2026-07-15) — extended channel enum covering target-first tiers (axis/target/indication/subtype) + modality tier. Rules opt into channels by including them as keys in the signals map. Channel-precedence at synthesis time: axis_fit → target_* → indication_fit_* → subtype_fit_* → modality_fit_*. Killers short-circuit within their own tier only. See target-contracts/docs/design/IDAS_SUBTYPE_PIPELINE.md.

tier_id.description: Which tier of the channel-precedence hierarchy this rule fires within. Optional; used by validators + synthesis-layer routing. Enforced iter-1 discipline: subtype-tier rules require subgroup metadata (see rule.subgroup_metadata_declared).

in_record_predicate.description: Phase 4 (2026-07-15; object-form added 2026-07-17) — Match records within a list-typed field. Used with card outputs like per_subgroup_metrics: [{stratum, class, subgroup_n, subgroup_n_floor_met, ...}]. The rule fires on a record when ALL key/value pairs in in_record match that record. Each map value is a scalar (exact match), an array (in-list match), or an object with an 'in' key (in-list match, explicit form). The subgroup-n floor is enforced declaratively by including `subgroup_n_floor_met: true` — an underpowered record simply fails the match, so an underpowered stratum is INADMISSIBLE by construction (cannot fire a verdict-affecting rule).

when.description: Predicate that matches the rule against a card's emitted descriptive label. Either scalar (equals/in) OR list-record (in_record) matching. card_id + field together identify which summary_field on which card to inspect.

field.description: The summary_field on the card to inspect.

signals.description: Map of signal_channel_id → signal_vocabulary. Each rule emits a signal for each listed channel. Channels not listed receive 'neutral' at the synthesis layer.

tier.description: Phase 4 (2026-07-15) optional tier annotation. Enables validator to enforce tier-specific requirements (e.g. subtype-tier rules must declare subgroup_metadata_declared).

emits.description: Phase 4 (2026-07-15) — Explicit declaration of which signal_vocabulary values this rule can emit. Enables coverage validators to reason about signal-absence semantics (insufficient vs not_applicable). Validator error if signals block emits a value NOT in this list.

subgroup_metadata_declared.description: Phase 4 (2026-07-15) — REQUIRED for subtype-tier rules (rule.tier == 'subtype'). Declares the subgroup-n floor discipline this rule respects. Validator error if a subtype-tier rule omits this or if any field is missing.

subgroup_n_source.description: Which resolver-manifest / cohort_size call sources the subgroup_n at rule-firing time (informational; runtime enforcement lives in the rule-firing layer).

min_n_required.description: Minimum subgroup_n for this rule to fire as 'supportive' rather than 'insufficient'. Default 30 unless overridden.

dominant.description: If true AND signal == supportive for a given channel, treated as a DOMINANT positive signal in Tier-3 scoring.

modality_importance.description: OPTIONAL (2026-07-23, modality-specific-interpretation / axis-2). Per-modality-channel IMPORTANCE weight for the question this rule answers (the spec's Critical/Important/Secondary/Irrelevant matrix). Keys are modality channels (the same enum as `signals`: small_molecule/degrader/adc/bite_tce/antibody); values are the weight. Lets a modality-fit gate (a) weight this rule's evidence and (b) flag when a CRITICAL question is UNANSWERABLE from the data (the rule fired `insufficient` on a channel it marks `critical`) → honest `insufficient`, not a silent pass. Additive metadata — inert to resolvers (which pattern-match rule_ids only), so it changes no verdict.

killer_message.description: Required when this rule fires a 'killer' signal.
